newsitem.title: MEXICO: FOCUS-Mexico's Carso buys Sears de Mexico.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Mexico's Carso buys Sears de Mexico.

text.p: Mexican holding company Grupo Carso SA on Wednesday agreed to buy a 60 percent stake of Sears, Roebuck and Co's Mexico unit, Sears de Mexico SA for $103 million.

Carso, run by Mexican billionaire Carlos Slim, would pay an average of about $2.2889 per share, or a 40 percent premium over the recent market price of Sears de Mexico shares, Sears said in a statement.
After the news, Sears shares on the Mexican Bolsa surged 20 percent to 17.80 pesos. Rumors of the sale in the past two days had pushed Sears share price up sharply already.
Shares of Grupo Carso, which has interests in everything from mining and cigarettes to retail, were also up 1.34 percent to 45.40 pesos shortly after the news.
Sears, which owned a 75 percent stake in Sears de Mexico, said it would keep a 15 percent interest in the troubled Mexican unit.
Sears de Mexico retains the right to use the Sears name in Mexico under exclusive license with a five-year initial term, Sears said.

"We are very pleased to form an alliance with a strong local partner...Grupo Carso has clearly signaled its intention to expand the number of Sears outlets, protect the Sears brand and grow the concept in Mexico," Sears Chairman and Chief Executive Arthur Martinez said in a statement.

Sears Roebuck and Co will retain representation on the board of Sears de Mexico. It said it expects to take a charge on the transaction in the first quarter, but the charge is not expected to have a material impact on annual earnings.
The transaction, subject to government approval in Mexico, will be completed in April.

Sears de Mexico was badly hit along with other retailers here by the country's economic crisis in 1994-1995. Economists expect Mexico's economic recovery this year to shore up flagging sales for retailers.

Carso's Slim, who also owns a controlling stake in Mexico's former telephone monopoly Telefonos de Mexico SA, has made a reputation in the Mexican business world for buying companies in trouble and turning them around.
Carso is Mexico's largest conglomerate and already owns cigarette company Cigatam, mining firm Frisco and Nacobre, copper wire-maker Condumex, retailer Sanborns, and tire maker Corporacion Llantera.

"The deal will have the most impact on the buyers, Carso, but first we need to analyze how they intend to pay for the deal and how compatible this new business line will be for Carso," a trader on the Mexican bourse said.
